comments.author: slesaad
comments.body: why was it not needed before? is this a lean mode concern?

comments.author: CarsonDavis
comments.body:
Not lean-specific — it's a "running behind a proxy" concern, and it's in this PR because the hardening batch is the mode-agnostic production-readiness set.

It wasn't needed before because the gap only shows up when something between the browser and the server reaps idle TCP connections. Local dev and same-host deployments have nothing in the middle, so a quiet WebSocket just stays open. Behind CloudFront → ALB (the lean admin topology), the ALB closes idle connections after ~60s of silence by default — and it does so without a clean close, so neither end notices. The two flows riding this socket (Configure lock warnings, layer-update push to open map clients) would silently stop working a minute after the last message, which is most of the time.

Any full deployment behind nginx/an ALB has the same latent issue today; it just hasn't had a deployment shape in-repo that put a proxy in front. Server-side ping/pong is the `ws` library's documented recommendation for exactly this (browsers auto-answer pings, so no client change). With `WEBSOCKET_PING_INTERVAL_MS` unset it defaults to 30s, and behavior is otherwise unchanged.
